items.body: Final confirmation uses `.chain(self.negative).find(|c| c.name == selected.name)`, losing the selected property’s category. An invariant and negative claim may legally share a name because their emitted operators have different prefixes. Selecting the negative claim then evaluates the invariant instead, potentially accepting a witness whose selected claim holds. Likewise, an authored invariant named `arithmetic` can make `ArithmeticSafe` return `Confirmation::Violation` without any arithmetic refusal.
items.suggestion: Dispatch by the selected property’s category and search only its corresponding native registrations. Require native arithmetic confirmation for `ArithmeticSafe`. Add regression tests for these name collisions.

items.body: The failure projection loses the state field’s integer type. `failure_projection` supplies an empty `visit`, so `for #binding in #domain { #visit }` no longer constrains the range through state construction. Unsuffixed literals default to `i32`. Consequently, a previously valid `#[starts(2147483648..=2147483648)] value: u64` fails compilation in the generated method, even without using Apalache. Narrow integer arithmetic can also evaluate at the wrong width and miss the native start refusal.
items.suggestion: Constrain each range binding to `#ty`, preserving the original expression inference. Add regression coverage for wide unsuffixed starts and width-sensitive arithmetic in start bounds.

items.body: Start-failure projection eagerly enumerates every preceding domain combination and stores every panic before replay can inspect the first result. For an outer `#[starts(0..=1000000000)]` followed by an overflowing start range, ordinary starts refuse immediately, but replay of a single initial arithmetic witness attempts to allocate a billion `StartFailure` entries. The decoder’s input limits do not bound this work.
items.suggestion: Validate the witness’s selected prefix directly, or make failure traversal lazy and bounded so replay can stop at the matching refusal.
